title: Three Caltrain reports kept the old rail operator fee ceiling

beats.text: Which fee could Caltrain’s rail operator earn? This is an investigative lead.

visual.sub: Staff distinguished the old performance-fee cap from a proposed new formula

beats.text: The old potential ceiling was $4.5 million a year.

visual.label: Staff distinguished the old performance-fee cap from a proposed new formula

beats.text: An amendment changed the terms from July 2022.

visual.kicker: The executed extension specified a new calculation from July 2022

beats.text: It specified a $2.8 million component adjusted for inflation, plus 2.8% of actual expenditures.

visual.kicker: The executed extension specified a new calculation from July 2022

beats.text: The signed inflation floor for overhead was 2.5%. The committee paper had given 3%.

visual.kicker: The executed extension specified a new calculation from July 2022

beats.text: The 2022 financial report covered the last year of the old terms.

visual.kicker: Three later financial statements continued to describe the old ceiling

beats.text: Three later annual reports still described a $4.5 million ceiling.
The 2025 report also said an outside consultant verified performance.

visual.kicker: Later amendments and the verification process leave the amount earned open

beats.text: The actual fee paid is still unknown.
Annual scorecards and invoices could explain which limit applied.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.

chapters.p: Staff distinguished the old performance-fee cap from a proposed new formula
chapters.b: The executed extension specified a new calculation from July 2022
chapters.o: Later amendments and the verification process leave the amount earned open
